increments.title: The break reaches the reviewer
increments.goal: The fact the test plan already determines — whether a criterion has a break, and what it is — travels out of the researcher's structured return and into the prompt of the reviewer that judges the increment.
criteria: The researcher's structured return names, for every acceptance criterion of the increment, whether the test plan named a break for it, and carries that break where it named one.
The workflow carries those criteria and their breaks into the prompt of the reviewer that judges the increment as a whole.
Each rule this increment adds to a page gets a case in `test-repo.sh` that turns red when that rule is removed.

increments.title: The reviewer executes the break and reads the unbreakable
increments.goal: The reviewer stops filing coverage findings against criteria no test can reach and judges them by reading the diff instead, and it stops trusting a named break: it applies each one in its sandbox and only a red run counts as verification.
criteria: The reviewer does not file the absence of a test for a criterion the researcher declared unbreakable.
The reviewer judges each unbreakable criterion by reading the diff against it, and says in its `summary` what it judged and on what.
The reviewer applies each named break in its sandbox worktree, runs the commands its prompt already names, and reports the criterion as verified only where that run fails.
A named break that leaves every one of those commands green is a finding against the criterion it was named for.
An applied break never reaches the checkout and never reaches the diff.
Each rule this increment adds to a page gets a case in `test-repo.sh` that turns red when that rule is removed.

increments.title: The run tells the human what was accepted unchecked
increments.goal: Every criterion an increment was accepted on without an executable check — including all of a `direct` increment's — comes back in the run result and reaches the human in the chat.
criteria: The run result carries, per increment, every criterion accepted without an executable check.
An increment worked `direct` names no break for any of its criteria, and the run result carries all of them as accepted without an executable check.
`rulebook.md` requires the session to give the human one line naming those criteria, for every increment that has any.
Each rule this increment adds to a page gets a case in `test-repo.sh` that turns red when that rule is removed.

steps.label: decompose

rulings: Cut the issue into three increments along the fact's path — determined, carried, acted on, reported — rather than one per criterion, because each of the three leaves the repository working on its own and every extra increment costs a full research-test-build-review chain; wrong costs one oversized increment that a later re-cut splits.

Kept the reviewer's two new duties, ignoring an unbreakable criterion's missing test and executing a named break, in one increment, because both are rules on the same page acting on the same fact and a reviewer that reads the fact for one purpose and not the other is half a change; wrong costs a larger review of agents/reviewer.md than either half alone.

Restated the issue's two run-wide criteria, a red-turning test-repo.sh case per added rule and `bash test.sh` exiting 0, in each increment scoped to that increment's own rules, because the alternative leaves the earlier increments landing untested rules; wrong costs the appearance of duplication in the backlog, not duplicated work.

Classified all three increments `full`, because each adds rules whose wording is not fixed by the criteria and each is required to land test-repo.sh cases that do not exist yet; wrong costs one research and one test dispatch on an increment that a direct chain would have finished.
return.summary: Three increments follow the fact's path: inc-1 makes the researcher's structured return carry, per criterion, whether the test plan named a break and what it is, and has the workflow carry those criteria and breaks into the reviewer's prompt; inc-2 gives the reviewer the two duties that fact enables, reading an unbreakable criterion against the diff instead of filing a coverage gap, and applying each named break in its sandbox so that only a red run verifies; inc-3 carries the criteria accepted without an executable check into the run result, covers the `direct` increment whose criteria are all of them, and makes rulebook.md require the session to name them to the human. Criterion mapping: researcher's return names the break per criterion -> inc-1; workflow carries criteria and breaks into the reviewer prompt -> inc-1; reviewer does not file an absent test for an unbreakable criterion -> inc-2; reviewer judges each unbreakable criterion against the diff and says so in its summary -> inc-2; reviewer applies each break in the sandbox and verifies only on a red run -> inc-2; a green break is a finding -> inc-2; an applied break never reaches the checkout or the diff -> inc-2; the run result carries the criteria accepted without an executable check -> inc-3; a direct increment names no break and all its criteria are carried -> inc-3; rulebook.md requires the human to be told -> inc-3; a red-turning test-repo.sh case per added rule -> inc-1, inc-2 and inc-3, each for its own rules; `bash test.sh` exits 0 -> inc-1, inc-2 and inc-3. I rejected a per-criterion cut of the reviewer's five criteria and a separate increment for the rulebook line, both of which buy four more agents for work one review can judge. The codemap names agents/researcher.md, agents/reviewer.md, workflows/agile-loop.js, rulebook.md and test-repo.sh; how the small return field is shaped so the projection stays cheap is a code fact inc-1's researcher settles, not a planning decision.

steps.prompt:
Issue directory: docs/issues/2026-08-16-the-break-decides-the-chain
Open the run state for docs/issues/2026-08-16-the-break-decides-the-chain/issue.md: map the issue against the codebase, decide the cut, and write both into docs/issues/2026-08-16-the-break-decides-the-chain/backlog.json with the `init` subcommand of the backlog helper your shared brief names, with workflow "agile-loop" and the whole codemap in the payload's `codemap` field.
This run works at most 8 increments, so a cut that needs more than that is a cut that is too fine.
Announce this step before you begin it and record it before you return, the way your shared brief describes, with the backlog helper it names:
  - `start docs/issues/2026-08-16-the-break-decides-the-chain/backlog.json - decompose <the prompt file>` — the prompt you were given, verbatim and whole, in a file outside the repository.
  - `record docs/issues/2026-08-16-the-break-decides-the-chain/backlog.json - decompose <the return file> <the prompt file>` — your return, in a file outside the repository, with that same prompt file. Commit it with your work and push the commit.
The fields your return carries, and your page says what each one holds:
  - `questions`
  - `rulings`
  - `summary`
